## Verified prior negative for the exact rectangle assertion

Problem 20001104 / AIM-COMBINATORICS-0229, original AIM Problem 2.4 and Croot–Lev §4.9.

At fixed δ=1/2 and C=1, the Boolean-cube/basis construction has |G|=mn/2 and |A+_G B|=m−1<m. Every rectangle retaining a fixed positive fraction c of each set has |A′+B′|≥(c²d/4)m for d≥4/c². Choosing d>max{2,4/c²,4K/c²} refutes the uniform K conclusion. The full signed base-3 construction, nonedge injection, Cauchy estimate and exact quantifier negation are retained.

This is verification and exposition of a known counterexample, not a new discovery. Green and Kane, [arXiv:1703.01036v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1703.01036v2), §4, page 5, records the cube/basis obstruction and credits Hosseini, Impagliazzo and Lovett. The proof supplies both the implication from that prior statement and a self-contained direct argument.

Only the precise ratio-free large-rectangle assertion is refuted. No assertion that every broader structural conclusion fails is made; bounded-imbalance results are compatible. No higher-density extension is included.

## Publication boundary and review limits

Exactly six authored proof/audit/acceptance and public-source-metadata files are added under `unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/20001104/`. All mathematical arguments and scope qualifications are preserved; the audit binds to the exact distributed proof. Only aggregate supplementary check metadata is retained, with no dependence on omitted computational files.

Scripts, fixtures, detailed computational output, datasets, copied third-party PDFs, extracted source text, page images and private coordination material are excluded. This AI-assisted, unrefereed edition makes no novelty, priority, external human peer-review, journal-acceptance or formal proof-assistant certification claim. Public scholarly inspection is recorded historical work; edition preparation rehashed the four available public PDFs without repeating scholarly retrieval or inspection.

QUEUE.md and unrelated entries are unchanged. Editorial preparation adds no substantive proof turn. No merge, release, DOI or outside outreach is requested.
